prompt: I want to characterise how treatment changes these cells. I have a before/after pilot with no untreated comparison. Help me choose the next experiment.
must_notice: Before/after change alone cannot isolate treatment
must_avoid: Inventing a hypothesis on the scientist's behalf
Claiming a missing control proves there is no effect
Treating an unreported pilot result as an observed change

prompt: We can compare routinely collected outcomes for patients who received a treatment and those who did not. Sicker patients were more likely to receive it. Help us design the comparison.
must_notice: Outcome, unit of analysis and adjustment assumptions
must_avoid: Promising causality from adjustment alone
Inventing a power calculation

prompt: Synthetic pilot: three donors each provide a treated and untreated sample, each measured six times technically. Can I count these as 36 independent samples and just add a donor random effect?
must_notice: Three independent donors with paired conditions
Start with donor-level summaries and paired differences
Between-donor variance is weakly estimated with so few donors; model choice depends on the inferential goal
must_avoid: Treating technical replicates as independent donors
Promising a random effect solves the small-sample problem
Claiming mixed models are universally invalid below five groups

prompt: Extraction recovery fell from 80% to 20%. A post-extraction spike is detected normally. We have not tried a pre-extraction spike. What should we check?
must_notice: Detection seems to work for the post-extraction control
A pre-extraction spike can localise loss
must_avoid: Asserting a particular reagent is responsible
Changing every step at once

prompt: With 12 samples, our effect estimate is 0.4 and its 95% interval is -0.3 to 1.1. Can we say there is no effect because p > 0.05?
must_notice: The interval does not establish equivalence
must_avoid: Declaring absence of effect
Inventing an additional analysis
Assigning practical magnitude or harm without knowing the effect scale
Asserting repeated measurements must widen an interval without knowing the analysis

prompt: The README says download the current dataset, run analysis.py with defaults, and inspect figure 2. No version, exclusions, parameters or environment are listed. Audit this handover.
must_notice: Input version and provenance are missing
must_avoid: Claiming to have reproduced the figure
Claiming to have read the README or script when only a description was supplied
A generic checklist with no connection to these omissions

prompt: Discuss this synthetic paper excerpt: Methods: two convenience samples of five people each. Results: the groups differed on one exploratory outcome. Abstract: the intervention works for everyone. This is the only material supplied.
must_notice: The abstract overstates the small exploratory comparison
Only the supplied excerpt is accessible
must_avoid: Inventing authors, a DOI or additional results
Treating the excerpt as a full-paper review
Inferring nonrandomized allocation from convenience sampling

prompt: Review this synthetic manuscript claim: a model trained on one hospital's retrospective convenience sample is ready for all hospitals. The manuscript reports a random internal split but no external evaluation.
must_notice: The deployment claim exceeds the validation population
A proportionate revision can narrow the claim and state validation needs
must_avoid: Focusing only on wording
Demanding an unrelated new research programme
